messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: measEq.syntax question
parts:
Hi, all.

I've got a 7-factor CFA with continuous indicators and two troup. I'm
trying to use semTools::measEq.syntax to create the nested models for
invariance testing (syntax for reprex is below).

The problem I'm running into is measEq.syntax seems to be giving two
components for each equation, one of them freed, regardless of the
level of invariance constraint. See the NA* entries:

E.g.:

> cat(mod.scalar)
## LOADINGS:

EN.Need =~ 1*EN.Personal.Need.6 + lambda.1_1*EN.Personal.Need.6
EN.Need =~ NA*EN.Family.Need.15 + lambda.2_1*EN.Family.Need.15
EN.Need =~ NA*EN.Culture.Need.24 + lambda.3_1*EN.Culture.Need.24
EN.Personal =~ 1*EN.Personal.Loved1 + lambda.4_2*EN.Personal.Loved1
EN.Personal =~ NA*EN.Personal.Exp.2 + lambda.5_2*EN.Personal.Exp.2
EN.Personal =~ NA*EN.Personal.Imp.5 + lambda.6_2*EN.Personal.Imp.5
...
## INTERCEPTS:

EN.Personal.Need.6 ~ 0*1 + nu.1*1
EN.Family.Need.15 ~ NA*1 + nu.2*1
EN.Culture.Need.24 ~ NA*1 + nu.3*1
EN.Personal.Loved1 ~ 0*1 + nu.4*1
EN.Personal.Exp.2 ~ NA*1 + nu.5*1
EN.Personal.Imp.5 ~ NA*1 + nu.6*1

The result is that all the models, when run, are effectively the
configural model. Can someone help me figure out what is going on?

Thanks,
Pat

library(lavaan)
library(semTools)

EN17.CFA <- '
EN.Need =~ EN.Personal.Need.6 + EN.Family.Need.15 + EN.Culture.Need.24
EN.Personal =~ EN.Personal.Loved1 + EN.Personal.Exp.2 + EN.Personal.Imp.5
EN.Culture =~ EN.Family.Enjoyed.10 + EN.Culture.Joy.23 + EN.Culture.Know.31
EN.Current =~ EN.Current.Personal.32 + EN.Current.Forward.35 +
EN.Current.PosExp.38 + EN.Current.Meprobs.43
EN.Art =~ En.Art.ImgSnow.46 + En.Art.Imgflks.47 +
EN.Art.PicLife.Snow.57 + EN.Art.PicLife.Play.58 +
EN.Art.PicLife.Trav.59 + EN.Art.PicLife.Work.60
EN.AtAv =~ EN.AtAv.Intrig.63 + EN.AtAv.Awe.64 + EN.AtAv.Unsafe.67
EN.Famil =~ EN.Famil.Safe.79 + EN.Famil.Belong.83 + EN.Famil.Exper.86
'

EN17.gender.config <- measEq.syntax(EN17.CFA,
group="Gender",ID.fac="auto.fix.first",meanstructure=TRUE)
mod.config <- as.character(EN17.gender.config)

EN17.gender.metric <- measEq.syntax(EN17.CFA, group="Gender",
group.equal="loadings", ID.fac="auto.fix.first", meanstructure=TRUE)
mod.metric <- as.character(EN17.gender.metric)

EN17.gender.scalar <- measEq.syntax(EN17.CFA, group="Gender",
group.equal=c("loadings","intercepts"), ID.fac="auto.fix.first",
meanstructure=TRUE)
mod.scalar <- as.character(EN17.gender.scalar)

cat(mod.config)
cat(mod.metric)
cat(mod.scalar)


--

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measEq.syntax question
parts:
The problem is that you are not giving it a data set, so the function doesnt know how many groups are in the variable "Gender"

add the argument data= ... and it will check how many groups do you have

Yes, this is necessary in the version on CRAN.  If you install the development version, I enabled a clumsy way to avoid needing raw data, using the sample.nobs= argument to specify an arbitrary vector whose length indicates the number of groups.

EN17.CFA <- '
EN.Need =~ EN.Personal.Need.6 + EN.Family.Need.15 + EN.Culture.Need.24
EN.Personal =~ EN.Personal.Loved1 + EN.Personal.Exp.2 + EN.Personal.Imp.5
EN.Culture =~ EN.Family.Enjoyed.10 + EN.Culture.Joy.23 + EN.Culture.Know.31
EN.Current =~ EN.Current.Personal.32 + EN.Current.Forward.35 +
              EN.Current.PosExp.38 + EN.Current.Meprobs.43
EN.Art =~ En.Art.ImgSnow.46 + En.Art.Imgflks.47 +
          EN.Art.PicLife.Snow.57 + EN.Art.PicLife.Play.58 +
          EN.Art.PicLife.Trav.59 + EN.Art.PicLife.Work.60
EN.AtAv =~ EN.AtAv.Intrig.63 + EN.AtAv.Awe.64 + EN.AtAv.Unsafe.67
EN.Famil =~ EN.Famil.Safe.79 + EN.Famil.Belong.83 + EN.Famil.Exper.86
'

EN17.gender.config <- measEq.syntax(EN17.CFA, group="Gender", sample.nobs=c(1,1),
                                    ID.fac="auto.fix.first", meanstructure=TRUE)
mod.config <- as.character(EN17.gender.config)
cat(mod.config) # there are now 2 values/labels per parameter

You could also do this with categorical data, but (if data= is missing) syntax would need to specify the correct number of thresholds.  If you are using lavaan to fit the model, there may not be any good reason to do it that way.  But as.character() is also intended to write Mplus syntax, in which case perhaps users don't want to fit models with lavaan.  

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measEq.syntax question
parts:
That would also get around having to specify a missing-data solution
in measEq.syntax, which I found I had to do because all cases have
some missing (it's an XABC planned missing structure).

Given the function's purpose is the generation of lavaan syntax, a practical solution would be to specify missing="fiml" or "pairwise" simply for the sake of fitting a template model to extract information about summary stats, etc.  But I agree that ideally, it would be unnecessary to do so, given that you are simply generating syntax (specifying the model), not yet fitting the model.  Perhaps I should add that consideration to the documentation.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
